blogs.title: Why 4‑Bit Is Enough: An Intuitive Guide to QLoRA’s NormalFloat Quantization
blogs.description: This post takes the reader through the idea that most LLM weights are normally distributed, explains the concept of NormalFloat (NF4), and shows why an information‑theoretic choice of a 4‑bit data type actually gives better results than the more common FP4 or Int4. It includes visualisations of quantisation bins, a comparison of error curves, and a quick demo that lets readers see the difference in perplexity on a small model.

blogs.title: Double‑Quantisation And Paged Optimisers: How QLoRA Keeps GPU Memory in Check
blogs.description: Here we peel back the three memory‑savings tricks that let you finetune a 65B LLM on a single 48GB GPU. The piece explains what the heavy block‑wise constants are, how packing them into a second quantised level saves ~0.37 bits per weight, and how NVIDIA unified memory + paged optimisers tame the shocking spikes that usually kill training. Readers walk away with a concrete checklist for making their own 4‑bit fine‑tuning jobs run.

blogs.title: From ChatGPT to Guanaco: How QLoRA Gives Open‑Source Models a Close‑Call Advantage
blogs.description: In this article we profile the Guanaco family – QLoRA‑finetuned on OASST1 – and why it reaches 99 % of ChatGPT on Vicuna while running on just a single consumer GPU. We trace experiment design, hyper‑parameter tweaks (e.g., fewer LoRA adapters per layer), and compare head‑to‑head Elo ratings versus human judgments to explain every little advantage Guanaco pulls off.

blogs.title: The Instruction Finetuning Spectrum: What Dataset Size Vs. Quality Really Means
blogs.description: This post examines the massive study of >1 000 instruction‐tuned models done with QLoRA. It shows how an 9K example OASST1 dataset can beat a 450K FLAN v2 split, discusses dataset stability over benchmarking venues (MMLU vs Vicuna vs OA), and offers practical guidelines for researchers looking to pick or create instruction corpora that maximise real chatbot performance.

blogs.title: Automated vs Human Chatbot Evaluation: Why GPT‑4 Ratings Are Cheaper but Not Perfect
blogs.description: We dive into the new tournament style Elo evaluation introduced by the authors, where GPT‑4 scores pairs of responses like a referee. The article explains how order effects, language ambiguity, and agreement metrics (Fleiss κ, Kendall τ) give a sense of reliability, and offers down‑to‑earth advice for anyone who wants to replace costly human reviews with inexpensive model‐based grading.

blogs.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Qualitative Lessons From Guanaco’s ‘Lemons and Cherries’ Responses
blogs.description: `Lemons` are intentionally bad answers that break a model; `cherries` show its best behavior. This blog walks readers through real examples – from factual recall mishaps to tricky refusal prompts – and explains how they reveal subtle shortcomings like math failures or theory of mind gaps that raw accuracy numbers hide.
